drugs.name: Gentamicin
drugs.uses: Gram-negative infections; synergy with a cell-wall-active agent for enterococcal/staphylococcal endocarditis; surgical prophylaxis.
drugs.adultDose: Traditional: 1–2.5mg/kg IV q8h. Extended-interval (preferred for most indications): 5–7mg/kg IV once daily. Surgical prophylaxis: weight-based (160/240/320mg for 45–64/65–74/75–85kg).
drugs.pedDose: 2.5mg/kg IV q8h (sepsis regimens in this guide); extended-interval dosing is age- and indication-dependent.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity (usually reversible), ototoxicity (vestibular and/or cochlear — can be irreversible), rare neuromuscular blockade.
drugs.monitoring: Serum creatinine; peak/trough or extended-interval nomogram levels; hearing assessment with prolonged courses.
drugs.notes: Restricted — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h.

drugs.name: Amikacin
drugs.uses: Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections; often retains activity when gentamicin resistance is present.
drugs.adultDose: 15mg/kg IV once daily (extended-interval), or 7.5mg/kg IV q12h (traditional).
drugs.pedDose: 15–20mg/kg/day, divided or once daily depending on age and indication.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, rare neuromuscular blockade.
drugs.monitoring: Renal function; peak/trough levels; hearing with prolonged use.
drugs.notes: Restricted — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h.

drugs.name: Fluconazole
drugs.uses: Candidiasis (oropharyngeal, esophageal, invasive) in susceptible species; cryptococcal infections.
drugs.action: Fungistatic against Candida (fungicidal against some other fungi).
drugs.adultDose: 100–800mg PO/IV once daily depending on indication (e.g. 100–200mg for oropharyngeal candidiasis per this guide; higher for invasive disease).
drugs.pedDose: 6–12mg/kg/day depending on indication.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, headache, hepatotoxicity (transaminitis), QT prolongation at high doses, rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
drugs.monitoring: LFTs with prolonged courses; ECG if combined with other QT-prolonging drugs.
drugs.renalAdj: Yes — dose reduction in renal impairment.
drugs.notes: Outside WHO AWaRe scope — AWaRe covers antibacterials only.

drugs.name: Caspofungin / Anidulafungin
drugs.uses: Invasive candidiasis, including azole-resistant species and empirical therapy in unstable/ICU patients.
drugs.action: Fungicidal against Candida; fungistatic against Aspergillus.
drugs.adultDose: Caspofungin: 70mg IV loading, then 50mg IV daily. Anidulafungin: 200mg IV loading, then 100mg IV daily.
drugs.pedDose: Weight-based — not detailed in this guide; consult pediatric ID/pharmacy.
drugs.sideEffects: Infusion reactions, transaminitis, fever, phlebitis.
drugs.monitoring: LFTs.
drugs.hepaticAdj: Caspofungin: dose reduction in moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B). Anidulafungin: no adjustment needed.
drugs.notes: Restricted — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h. Outside AWaRe scope.

drugs.name: Nystatin
drugs.uses: Mild oropharyngeal candidiasis.
drugs.pkpd: Not clinically applicable — minimal systemic absorption.
drugs.adultDose: 400,000–600,000 units (4–6mL) PO, swish and swallow/spit, QID.
drugs.pedDose: 100,000–400,000 units QID depending on age.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset (rare, minimal absorption), unpleasant taste.
drugs.monitoring: None routinely needed.
drugs.notes: Outside AWaRe scope.

drugs.name: Acyclovir / Valacyclovir
drugs.uses: HSV and VZV infections — encephalitis, retinitis, mucocutaneous/genital disease.
drugs.action: Virustatic — inhibits viral DNA polymerase, halting replication; does not eradicate latent virus.
drugs.pkpd: Time above IC50 (T>IC50) — the antiviral analogue of time-dependent antibacterial killing.
drugs.adultDose: Acyclovir: 400mg PO q8h (initial genital herpes); 800mg PO q8h ×2 days (recurrent episode); 10mg/kg IV q8h (severe disease/encephalitis, per guide). Valacyclovir: 1000mg PO q8h (oral step-down).
drugs.pedDose: 10–20mg/kg IV q8h for HSV encephalitis (age-dependent) — not fully detailed in this guide; consult pediatric ID.
drugs.sideEffects: Renal impairment (crystalline nephropathy, especially IV/rapid infusion/dehydration), nausea, headache, rare neurotoxicity/confusion (especially with renal impairment or in the elderly).
drugs.monitoring: Renal function; ensure adequate hydration during IV therapy.
drugs.notes: Outside AWaRe scope.

drugs.name: Ganciclovir / Valganciclovir
drugs.uses: CMV infections, particularly retinitis in immunocompromised patients.
drugs.pkpd: T>IC50 (AUC also correlates with both efficacy and myelosuppression risk).
drugs.adultDose: Ganciclovir 5mg/kg IV q12h (induction, per guide), then Valganciclovir 900mg PO once daily (maintenance, per guide).
drugs.pedDose: Weight-based — CMV treatment in children is specialized; consult pediatric ID.
drugs.sideEffects: Myelosuppression (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia — most significant), nephrotoxicity, GI upset.
drugs.monitoring: CBC (weekly or more frequently), renal function.
drugs.notes: Outside AWaRe scope.

drugs.name: Oseltamivir
drugs.uses: Influenza A and B — treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis.
drugs.action: Virustatic — blocks neuraminidase-mediated release of virus from infected cells.
drugs.pkpd: Not classically defined via an MIC-based framework; dosing based on trial-established systemic exposure.
drugs.adultDose: 75mg PO BD ×5 days.
drugs.pedDose: Weight-based (per guide): 2wks–11mo 3mg/kg/12h; ≤15kg 30mg/12h; >15–23kg 45mg/12h; >23–40kg 60mg/12h; >40kg 75mg/12h.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, headache; rare neuropsychiatric events (mainly reported in pediatric/adolescent patients).
drugs.monitoring: None routinely required.
drugs.notes: Outside AWaRe scope.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.uses: Streptococcal pharyngitis, otitis media, sinusitis, dental endocarditis prophylaxis.
drugs.adultDose: 500mg PO q8h.
drugs.pedDose: 50mg/kg once daily (max 1000–1200mg, pharyngitis); 80–90mg/kg/day divided q8–12h (acute otitis media).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset (diarrhea), rash (including non-allergic ampicillin-class rash), rare hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis.
drugs.monitoring: None routine; watch for rash/allergic reaction.
drugs.renalAdj: Yes — dose reduction in severe impairment.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate
drugs.uses: Broad-spectrum coverage including beta-lactamase-producing organisms — respiratory infections, skin/soft tissue, UTI, animal bites.
drugs.adultDose: 1g PO BD (875/125mg) for most indications; 1750/250mg (2 tabs) for surgical prophylaxis.
drugs.pedDose: 45mg/kg/day divided q12h (pharyngitis/tonsillitis); 90/6.4mg/kg/day divided q12h extra-strength (AOM).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset (diarrhea more common than amoxicillin alone), hepatotoxicity (cholestatic, can be delayed onset), rash.
drugs.monitoring: LFTs if prolonged course or symptoms of hepatotoxicity.
drugs.hepaticAdj: Caution — avoid/monitor if prior amoxicillin-clavulanate-associated hepatotoxicity.

drugs.name: Ampicillin
drugs.uses: Listeria, Enterococcus (often with gentamicin for endocarditis), Group B strep.
drugs.adultDose: 2g IV q4h (endocarditis, Listeria, Enterococcus).
drugs.pedDose: 150–200mg/kg/day IV divided q6–8h (sepsis/CAP/meningitis — varies by age/indication in this guide).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash (including non-allergic rash, especially with concurrent viral infection e.g. EBV), rare anaphylaxis.
drugs.monitoring: None routine.

drugs.name: Cloxacillin
drugs.uses: MSSA bacteremia, endocarditis, skin/soft tissue infections.
drugs.adultDose: 2g IV q4h.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — consult pediatric reference (typical 25–50mg/kg/dose q6h).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, rare hepatotoxicity, interstitial nephritis.
drugs.monitoring: Renal function/LFTs with prolonged high-dose IV therapy.

drugs.name: Piperacillin-Tazobactam
drugs.uses: Broad-spectrum coverage including Pseudomonas; polymicrobial and intra-abdominal infections.
drugs.adultDose: 4.5g IV q6–8h (extended infusion often used to maximize T>MIC).
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — consult pediatric reference (typical 100mg/kg/dose piperacillin component q6–8h).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, hypokalemia, elevated LFTs, interstitial nephritis, increased AKI risk especially with vancomycin.
drugs.monitoring: Renal function (especially if combined with vancomycin), electrolytes, LFTs.
drugs.notes: See Drug Interaction Checker for the vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam AKI signal.

drugs.name: Benzathine Penicillin G
drugs.uses: Syphilis; GAS pharyngitis when injectable therapy is preferred.
drugs.pkpd: %T>MIC — depot release sustains T>MIC over weeks.
drugs.adultDose: 2.4 million units IM single dose (primary syphilis); weekly ×3 doses (late latent).
drugs.pedDose: Weight-based — not detailed in this guide.
drugs.sideEffects: Injection site pain/induration, rare anaphylaxis, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction (syphilis treatment).
drugs.monitoring: Observe for anaphylaxis post-injection; serologic follow-up for syphilis.
drugs.notes: IM only — never administer IV (risk of embolic/vasospastic reaction).

drugs.name: Cefazolin
drugs.uses: Surgical prophylaxis; MSSA infections.
drugs.adultDose: 2g IV q8h (treatment); 2g IV (3g if >120kg) for surgical prophylaxis.
drugs.pedDose: 30mg/kg IV (surgical prophylaxis); 50mg/kg for dental IE prophylaxis.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, phlebitis at infusion site, rare hypersensitivity (penicillin cross-reactivity is low, ~1–2%).
drugs.monitoring: None routine.

drugs.name: Cefuroxime
drugs.uses: Respiratory tract infections, uncomplicated UTI.
drugs.adultDose: 500mg PO BD.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide for treatment — consult pediatric reference.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, rare hepatotoxicity.
drugs.monitoring: None routine.

drugs.name: Cefotaxime
drugs.uses: Meningitis, community-acquired pneumonia, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
drugs.adultDose: 2g IV q8h (varies by indication; higher-frequency dosing used for meningitis).
drugs.pedDose: 50mg/kg q6–8h (meningitis); 150mg/kg/day divided q8h (CAP).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, rare hepatotoxicity/nephrotoxicity.
drugs.monitoring: None routine.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.uses: Broad empirical use — CAP, meningitis, gonorrhea, many Gram-negative and streptococcal infections.
drugs.adultDose: 2g IV once daily (most indications); 1g IM single dose (STI); 2g IV single dose (surgical prophylaxis).
drugs.pedDose: 50–100mg/kg IV/IM once daily depending on indication.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, biliary sludging/pseudolithiasis (especially prolonged high-dose use), rash, rare hemolytic anemia.
drugs.monitoring: Consider gallbladder ultrasound if prolonged high-dose therapy with symptoms.
drugs.hepaticAdj: Caution in combined severe renal + hepatic impairment.
drugs.notes: Do not co-administer IV with calcium-containing solutions in neonates.

drugs.name: Cefixime
drugs.uses: Pediatric UTI, gonorrhea.
drugs.adultDose: Not routinely used in adults in this guide.
drugs.pedDose: 8mg/kg PO once daily (UTI).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset (diarrhea more common than other oral cephalosporins), rash.
drugs.monitoring: None routine.

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.uses: Nosocomial infections including Pseudomonas, febrile neutropenia, HAP/VAP.
drugs.adultDose: 2g IV q8h.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — consult pediatric reference (typical 50mg/kg/dose q8h).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, seizures, myoclonus — especially with renal impairment and inadequate dose adjustment), rare hepatotoxicity.
drugs.monitoring: Renal function (adjust dose promptly); watch for neurotoxicity in renal impairment/elderly.
drugs.renalAdj: Yes — critical (neurotoxicity risk if not adjusted).
drugs.tdm: Not routine (emerging in critically ill/renal impairment).

drugs.name: Meropenem
drugs.uses: ESBL-producing and other resistant Gram-negative infections; severe polymicrobial infections.
drugs.adultDose: 1g IV q8h (extended infusion often used).
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed for general treatment in this guide — consult pediatric reference (typical 20–40mg/kg/dose q8h).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, rare seizures (especially with renal impairment/high doses/CNS disease), elevated LFTs.
drugs.monitoring: Renal function; neurologic status in high-risk patients.
drugs.notes: Restricted — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h. Reduces valproate levels — see Drug Interaction Checker.

drugs.name: Ertapenem
drugs.uses: Community-acquired complicated infections, ESBL organisms; once-daily dosing convenience.
drugs.adultDose: 1g IV once daily.
drugs.pedDose: 15mg/kg BD, max 1g/day — standard reference dosing, not detailed in this guide.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash, phlebitis, rare seizures.
drugs.monitoring: Renal function.
drugs.notes: Restricted (MOH) — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h. Reduces valproate levels — see Drug Interaction Checker.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.uses: Gram-negative infections including Pseudomonas; UTI; gastrointestinal infections.
drugs.pkpd: AUC24/MIC, target ~125 for Gram-negatives; Cmax/MIC also correlates.
drugs.adultDose: 500mg PO BD, or 400mg IV BD.
drugs.pedDose: 10mg/kg IV/PO (varies by indication).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, tendinopathy/tendon rupture, QT prolongation, CNS effects (headache, dizziness, rare seizures), dysglycemia, rare peripheral neuropathy (can be irreversible), photosensitivity.
drugs.monitoring: Blood glucose if diabetic; tendon symptoms; ECG if other QT risk factors present.
drugs.notes: Carries boxed warnings for tendinopathy, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, and myasthenia gravis exacerbation — avoid in myasthenia gravis.

drugs.name: Levofloxacin
drugs.uses: CAP, UTI; broader Gram-positive/S. pneumoniae coverage than ciprofloxacin.
drugs.pkpd: AUC24/MIC, target ~30–40 for Gram-positives, ~125 for Gram-negatives.
drugs.adultDose: 750mg PO/IV once daily (most indications); 500mg for some indications.
drugs.pedDose: 10mg/kg — fluoroquinolones are generally used sparingly in children; limited to select indications.
drugs.sideEffects: Same class effects as ciprofloxacin (tendinopathy, QT prolongation, CNS effects, dysglycemia, photosensitivity).
drugs.monitoring: Same as ciprofloxacin.
drugs.notes: Same class boxed warnings as ciprofloxacin.

drugs.name: Moxifloxacin
drugs.uses: CAP, polymicrobial infections with enhanced Gram-positive/anaerobic activity.
drugs.adultDose: 400mg PO/IV once daily.
drugs.pedDose: Not used routinely in pediatrics in this guide.
drugs.sideEffects: Same class effects; highest QT-prolongation risk of the fluoroquinolone class.
drugs.monitoring: ECG if other QT risk factors/drugs present.
drugs.renalAdj: Not required — unique among fluoroquinolones (hepatically cleared).
drugs.notes: Same class boxed warnings as ciprofloxacin.

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.uses: MRSA and other serious Gram-positive infections; oral formulation for C. difficile.
drugs.action: Bactericidal against most Gram-positives — but bacteriostatic against Enterococcus (hence combined with an aminoglycoside for enterococcal endocarditis).
drugs.adultDose: 15–20mg/kg IV q8–12h (loading dose 20–25mg/kg for serious MRSA infections, then per levels); 1g IV BD (≤90kg)/1.5g IV BD (>90kg) for prophylaxis; oral 125mg q6h for C. difficile.
drugs.pedDose: 15mg/kg IV q6–8h (varies by age/indication).
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, Vancomycin Flushing Syndrome (infusion-related, histamine-mediated — not a true allergy), rare ototoxicity at modern dosing, thrombophlebitis, rare DRESS syndrome.
drugs.monitoring: AUC24 (preferred, via trough or 2-level sampling) or trough level; renal function, especially with prolonged courses or nephrotoxic co-therapy.
drugs.notes: Restricted — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h. See Drug Interaction Checker for piperacillin-tazobactam/aminoglycoside AKI risk.

drugs.name: Daptomycin
drugs.uses: Complicated MRSA bacteremia/endocarditis; vancomycin-resistant Gram-positive infections.
drugs.pkpd: Cmax/MIC and AUC/MIC (both correlate with efficacy).
drugs.adultDose: 6mg/kg IV once daily (bacteremia/endocarditis); higher doses (8–10mg/kg) used for some resistant infections — not detailed per-indication in this guide.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — specialist or ID/Clinical Microbiology contact required.
drugs.sideEffects: Myopathy/CK elevation (dose-dependent), rare eosinophilic pneumonia (important — do not use for pneumonia), GI upset, injection site reactions.
drugs.monitoring: Weekly CK (creatine kinase), renal function.
drugs.renalAdj: Yes — extend dosing interval in renal impairment.
drugs.notes: Restricted. Inactivated by pulmonary surfactant — not effective for pneumonia. See Drug Interaction Checker for statin interaction.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.uses: Atypical pneumonia coverage, chlamydia, pertussis.
drugs.action: Bacteriostatic (can be bactericidal at high concentrations against some organisms).
drugs.adultDose: 500mg PO/IV once daily, or 500mg ×1 then 250mg once daily ×4 days (varies by indication).
drugs.pedDose: 10mg/kg once daily (duration varies by indication).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset (most common), QT prolongation, rare hepatotoxicity, reversible hearing loss at high cumulative doses.
drugs.monitoring: ECG if other QT risk factors present; generally well tolerated.
drugs.notes: Carries an FDA cardiovascular boxed warning for QT prolongation/sudden cardiac death risk in patients with pre-existing cardiac risk factors.

drugs.name: Clarithromycin
drugs.uses: H. pylori therapy (combination regimens), atypical pneumonia coverage, pharyngitis alternative.
drugs.adultDose: 500mg PO BD.
drugs.pedDose: 15mg/kg/day divided q12h.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset (more common than azithromycin), metallic taste, QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity.
drugs.monitoring: ECG if other QT risk factors present; LFTs with prolonged use.
drugs.renalAdj: Yes — dose reduction in severe impairment.
drugs.notes: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor — extensive interaction potential (statins, colchicine) — see Drug Interaction Checker.

drugs.name: Clindamycin
drugs.uses: Anaerobic infections; toxin-suppression adjunct in necrotizing fasciitis/toxic shock; skin/soft tissue MRSA where local resistance is low.
drugs.action: Bacteriostatic (can be bactericidal at higher concentrations against some strains).
drugs.adultDose: 600–900mg IV q8h (severe infections); 300–450mg PO q8h (oral).
drugs.pedDose: 10mg/kg IV/PO q8h (varies by indication).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, C. difficile-associated diarrhea (notably higher risk than most other antibiotics), rash.
drugs.monitoring: Watch for diarrhea — assess for C. difficile if it develops.
drugs.notes: One of the antibiotics most strongly associated with C. difficile infection.

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.uses: Atypical pneumonia, tick-borne illness, some STIs, broad-spectrum oral alternative.
drugs.adultDose: 100mg PO BD.
drugs.pedDose: Generally avoided <8 years (tooth discoloration) except select indications (e.g. severe rickettsial disease).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, esophagitis (take with adequate water, remain upright), photosensitivity, tooth discoloration (children <8y or in utero exposure).
drugs.monitoring: None routine.
drugs.renalAdj: Not required — safe in renal impairment, unlike older tetracyclines.
drugs.notes: Avoid in pregnancy and children under 8 years.

drugs.name: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole
drugs.uses: UTI, Pneumocystis pneumonia (treatment and prophylaxis), MRSA skin/soft tissue infections.
drugs.action: Each component is individually bacteriostatic; the combination is bactericidal (sequential folate-pathway blockade).
drugs.adultDose: 1–2 DS tablets PO BD (varies by indication); higher dose (15–20mg/kg/day trimethoprim component, divided) for PCP treatment.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed for general treatment in this guide beyond specific protocols — consult pediatric reference.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, rash (including rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome/TEN), hyperkalemia, bone marrow suppression (especially with folate deficiency), crystalluria (ensure hydration).
drugs.monitoring: Renal function, potassium, CBC with prolonged/high-dose use (e.g. PCP treatment).
drugs.notes: See Drug Interaction Checker for methotrexate/warfarin/ACE-ARB interactions.

drugs.name: Metronidazole
drugs.uses: Anaerobic infections, C. difficile (alternative agent), protozoal infections, part of H. pylori regimens.
drugs.adultDose: 500mg PO/IV q8h (varies by indication); 500mg PO q12h (bacterial vaginosis).
drugs.pedDose: 15mg/kg IV/PO (varies by indication).
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, metallic taste, peripheral neuropathy (with prolonged use), disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, rare seizures/encephalopathy (prolonged/high-dose use).
drugs.monitoring: Neurologic symptoms with prolonged courses.
drugs.hepaticAdj: Yes — dose reduction in severe impairment.
drugs.notes: Avoid alcohol during and for 48 hours after treatment.

drugs.name: Nitrofurantoin
drugs.uses: Uncomplicated lower UTI/cystitis only.
drugs.action: Bactericidal at the concentrations achieved in urine.
drugs.pkpd: Urinary concentration-dependent — not a classic serum-MIC-based index.
drugs.adultDose: 100mg PO BD.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed for routine treatment in this guide.
drugs.sideEffects: GI upset, pulmonary toxicity (acute, and rare chronic/fibrotic with long-term use), hepatotoxicity, rare peripheral neuropathy, hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency.
drugs.monitoring: Pulmonary symptoms with prolonged/repeated courses; avoid in G6PD deficiency.
drugs.renalAdj: Avoid if CrCl <30–60mL/min — reduced efficacy and increased toxicity risk.
drugs.notes: Does not achieve therapeutic tissue/blood levels — not for pyelonephritis or systemic infection.

drugs.name: Linezolid
drugs.uses: VRE, MRSA (particularly when vancomycin is not tolerated or failing); good lung/soft-tissue penetration.
drugs.action: Bacteriostatic against staphylococci and enterococci; bactericidal against most streptococci.
drugs.adultDose: 600mg PO/IV q12h.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — consult pediatric ID/pharmacy.
drugs.sideEffects: Myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia most common, especially with courses >2 weeks), peripheral/optic neuropathy with prolonged use, rare lactic acidosis.
drugs.monitoring: CBC weekly (especially if course >2 weeks); visual symptoms if prolonged use.
drugs.notes: Restricted. Weak MAO-inhibitor activity — see Drug Interaction Checker for serotonergic interactions.

drugs.name: Colistin
drugs.uses: Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections (Acinetobacter, Pseudomonas, CRE) — a last-line agent.
drugs.adultDose: Weight- and renal-function-based per the Nation 2017 look-up table method (see Colistin Dosing calculator) — loading dose (4×weight, max 300 mg CBA) then maintenance by CrCl band, starting 12h after loading.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — specialist or ID/Clinical Microbiology contact required.
drugs.sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity (dose-limiting, common), neurotoxicity (paresthesias, dizziness, rare neuromuscular blockade/respiratory paralysis).
drugs.monitoring: Renal function closely (frequent, e.g. daily to every-other-day); neurologic symptoms.
drugs.renalAdj: Dosing is inherently renal-function-based — see calculator.
drugs.tdm: Emerging in specialized centers, not yet routine.
drugs.notes: Restricted (MOH) — ID / Clinical Microbiology approval required beyond 24h.

drugs.name: Rifampin
drugs.uses: Adjunctive therapy for prosthetic device/biofilm infections — always combined with another active agent, never as monotherapy.
drugs.adultDose: Typical adjunctive dose 300–600mg PO BD — not detailed per-indication in this guide beyond its adjunctive role.
drugs.pedDose: Not detailed in this guide — consult pediatric ID/pharmacy.
drugs.sideEffects: Orange discoloration of body fluids (harmless — counsel patient), hepatotoxicity, GI upset, flu-like reaction with intermittent dosing, rare thrombocytopenia.
drugs.monitoring: LFTs, CBC with prolonged use.
drugs.notes: Never use as monotherapy — resistance emerges rapidly. Potent CYP3A4/2C9 inducer — see Drug Interaction Checker.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function and drug levels closely; avoid prolonged combination if an alternative regimen is reasonable.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function and drug levels closely; avoid prolonged combination if an alternative regimen is reasonable.

interactions.mechanism: Combination is associated with a higher rate of acute kidney injury than either agent alone (well documented in recent literature).
interactions.management: Monitor renal function closely; consider an alternative combination (e.g. vancomycin + cefepime) if baseline AKI risk is high.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function closely.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Avoid combination if possible; monitor renal function closely if unavoidable.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Avoid combination if possible; monitor renal function closely if unavoidable.

interactions.mechanism: No added antibacterial benefit from combining two aminoglycosides; additive nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity.
interactions.management: Avoid combining two aminoglycosides.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampin induces fluconazole metabolism, reducing antifungal levels.
interactions.management: Consider dose adjustment or an alternative antifungal; monitor for treatment failure.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampin may reduce doxycycline levels via enzyme induction.
interactions.management: Monitor clinical response; consider an alternative if concurrent use is required long-term.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampin induces clarithromycin metabolism, reducing macrolide levels; clarithromycin may also increase rifampin levels.
interactions.management: Consider an alternative macrolide (e.g. azithromycin, which is not a significant CYP substrate) if long-term concurrent use is needed.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampin induces metabolism, reducing caspofungin levels.
interactions.management: An increased caspofungin dose may be needed; monitor for antifungal treatment failure.

interactions.mechanism: Documented seizure risk when carbapenems are combined with ganciclovir/valganciclovir (most robust data is with imipenem-cilastatin; extrapolated caution applies to meropenem).
interactions.management: Avoid combination if possible; if unavoidable, monitor closely for seizures.

interactions.mechanism: Documented seizure risk when carbapenems are combined with ganciclovir/valganciclovir (most robust data is with imipenem-cilastatin; extrapolated caution applies to ertapenem).
interactions.management: Avoid combination if possible; if unavoidable, monitor closely for seizures.

interactions.mechanism: Additive oto- and nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function and hearing; use lowest effective doses of both.

interactions.mechanism: Aminoglycosides can enhance neuromuscular blockade.
interactions.management: Use caution perioperatively; monitor for prolonged paralysis/respiratory depression.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function closely.

interactions.mechanism: Additive oto- and nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function and hearing; use lowest effective doses of both.

interactions.mechanism: Aminoglycosides can enhance neuromuscular blockade.
interactions.management: Use caution perioperatively; monitor for prolonged paralysis/respiratory depression.

interactions.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor renal function closely.

interactions.mechanism: May enhance the anticoagulant effect.

criteria: Implanted foreign material infection (e.g. prosthetic cardiac valve)
Positive follow-up blood culture drawn > 48 h after starting therapy
Deep-seated focus, septic embolism, or other metastatic focus
Continuous fever > 48–72 h after starting effective therapy
mdroCrit: Admitted to ICU (except transient post-surgical observation for a few hours)
Hospital admission with previous MRSA / MDR Gram-negative colonisation or infection
Going for a high-risk surgical procedure
Going for a surgical implantation procedure
mdroRisk: Recent / recurrent hospital admission or surgery
Foreign body, invasive device, or instrumentation
Travel to / referral from a high-MDRO centre
